text:
Texas Tech alumni represented on 17 NFL teams for preseason week one
W. F. Castro
Texas Tech University has 24 former players on National Football League rosters entering the first weekend of the 2026 preseason, with a program-best nine Red Raiders selected in the most recent NFL Draft, according to an Aug. 12 announcement from Texas Tech Athletics.
Of the league's 32 franchises, Texas Tech alumni are present on 17 teams. The Miami Dolphins have the highest concentration with three former Red Raiders: linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, drafted in the second round (No. 43 overall); wide receiver Caleb Douglas, taken in the third round (No. 75 overall); and All-Pro linebacker Jordyn Brooks, who is beginning his seventh season.
The annual Hall of Fame Game on Aug. 6 featured two of this year's draft picks as the Carolina Panthers defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 33-30. Wide receiver Reggie Virgil led Arizona with five receptions for 66 yards on six targets after being picked by the Cardinals in the fifth round. Safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson also played for Arizona as he enters his third NFL season following his fourth-round selection in a previous draft. For Carolina, defensive tackle Lee Hunter—chosen No. 49 overall—played twenty snaps and recorded one tackle.
Among veteran players, three-time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Patrick Mahomes II is set to begin his tenth season as quarterback for the Kansas City Chiefs. Offensive tackle Terence Steele (Dallas Cowboys) and Jordyn Brooks both enter their seventh seasons.
NFL clubs must reduce their rosters to a maximum of fifty-three players by August 30 at six p.m., following completion of a three-game preseason schedule that concludes prior to that date. Practice squads can be established starting August 31 and will include up to seventeen players per team; final training camp days end September 6 before Kickoff Weekend begins September 9-14.
